data.name: Lifestream - A Haunting Text Adventure
data.detailed_description:
Lifestream is a haunting tribute to the classic text adventure that plunges players into the roles of Randolph and John Holton, a father and son desperate for answers to the mysteries surrounding a mysterious realm and an enigmatic brotherhood.

Gameplay

Lifestream is a modern "blast from the past" that combines the best elements of interactive fiction, visual novels, and gamebooks with a graphic user interface that emulates the look of early 1990s text adventures. It features beautiful artwork and cinematic music. In place of a text parser is a context-specific multiple choice menu. A compass allows you to travel from room to room, and separate inventory, map, journal, and character screens are available at the push of a button.

Lifestream plays like an interactive novel. You make a series of choices that determine what happens next in the story. But unlike traditional gamebooks and choose-your-own adventures, Lifestream also features more advanced adventure game mechanics, including locations to explore, items to collect and use, characters to meet and interact with, and puzzles to solve.

Story

"Father Randolph Holton was dead. Not literally, of course. But in his heart, he knew he could not live on...not after everything he had learned. Sitting at his dark oak desk in the corner of the dimly lit, cozy study, the white-haired, frail Catholic priest--even frailer of late--dipped an old quill into a container of jet-black ink and began to write..."

John Holton's father, a Catholic priest named Randolph, has been missing for two weeks. Unable to go to the police for help, since doing so would tarnish his father's reputation as a celibate priest, John takes it upon himself to search for his father.

Over the course of Lifestream, players take on the roles of both John in the present and his father, Randolph, in the past. While John searches for answers, players see the troubling events that led to Randolph's disappearance firsthand.

Features

  • EXPLORE multiple detailed locations, including a quaint Victorian home and small village church
  • ENJOY over 150 pieces of original artwork
  • SOLVE a multitude of challenging puzzles
  • INTERACT with a variety of interesting characters
  • EXPERIENCE an emotional, hour-long soundtrack
  • UNLOCK 30 achievements to view a special post-game bonus scene
  • PLAY 8+ hours of content with over 78,000 words--the text equivalent of a full-length novel!

data.short_description: Find your missing father and uncover the dark conspiracy surrounding a sacred artifact and an enigmatic brotherhood in this haunting text adventure that combines the best elements of classic interactive fiction and gamebooks.

reviews.review:
A text-based interactive adventure with many twists and turns of events, this game didn't fail to make me gasp and startle in some of the scenes. The story starts when John Holton, a young man whose father has disappeared and he wanted to investigate his disappearance. Sounds normal right? The twist is, John's father is a Catholic priest named Randolph, an old man who you can make either nice or grumpy depends on your choices.  Since John's father is a priest, the young man couldn't get help from anyone, not even the police. So he decided to search for his father alone. You'll be taken to the past and present as you progress into the story to learn more about the disappearance, You'll play as both John and Randolph to discover even a deeper and darker secret and a real twist by the end of the game.

The atmosphere and music worked wonderfully with the story which was written beautifully. I liked the map, although you can't fast travel in it, the navigation and how it was designed made moving around easy. Each location was described nicely and had many things to interact with.
http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1320678643 

While the story started slow, it was a great foundation for what comes next as everything starts to make sense. This game requires a lot of reading, you can't skip anything, even the notes you find scattered around, they work as clues for the puzzles you encounter. Those puzzles vary from hard to easy, and each one has done creatively. I liked the one with the woman, child and man voices which leads you to the right path, it was an amazing and creepy puzzle. 
While this game is older than Shady Brook, I found the characters design here more appealing, and the design of the house was nicely done.
http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1308676043

Although the game not entirely connected to the other games by the same developer, I liked the mention of the other characters in the other games, makes it feel like it is the same universe. You can learn more about each character from the codex on the official website, but I encourage you not to do so before finishing the game as it gives huge spoilers of the characters. 
And of course, we can't deny that the pointing system is a good feature of the game.
http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1320770120

Pros:
+Nice artwork, characters design looks good, especially Randolph and his son.
+Interesting dark and creepy story.
+Good music and atmosphere.
+Very well-written story.
+Good map (no fast travel feature).
+Gamebook style.
+Detective theme.
+Choices matters.
+Interesting characters and tons of creepy ones too.
+Points system.
+Good challenging and creative puzzles.
+Steam achievements.

Cons:
-No option for voice-overs. (Would be nice if the character say a word or two, not the whole paragraph)
-Lots of backtracking.

Again, this game is not for everyone, this is a novel game which requires long hours of reading and exploring-  I love that and wish for more games of this genre. I do recommend it to people who love to read like me! You can't miss this dark adventure!
